name: The Hanover Insurance Group, Inc.
reason: Commercial/personal-lines P&C underwriter whose EPS ($19.09) is 1.0x its 10y max after a hard-market repricing, with a -72% cat-driven year in 2023, 2.7%/yr revenue growth and consensus FY2-FY3 EPS of -4%/+3%, so current earnings look near an underwriting-cycle peak with no route to >=7%/yr.

name: Rapid7, Inc.
reason: Sub-scale vulnerability-management/SIEM vendor with 10y avg ROIC -36%, shares +10%/yr, ND/EBITDA 8.6x, adjusted EPS ~5x GAAP and consensus FY1 EPS -13.5% amid platform consolidation by larger security vendors.

name: Visteon Corp.
reason: Net-cash cockpit-electronics supplier but earnings are set by global auto production and OEM program wins (EPS swung 0.97 to 17.68 to 7.75 in five years, 0.44x 10y max, 1.5%/yr revenue CAGR), which cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: EPAM Systems, Inc.
reason: Strong net-cash record (10y EPS CAGR 15.5%, revenue CAGR 19.6%) but EBIT margin has compressed to 9.2% (9th pctile) and EPS growth has stalled since 2022, as AI-driven coding productivity is a credible threat to labour-based digital-engineering pricing within 5 years.

name: Provident Financial Services, Inc.
reason: Ordinary NJ thrift with 10y avg ROE 8.3%, 10y EPS CAGR 5.3% and shares +7.5%/yr from the Lakeland merger; a spread-dependent lender with no specialness and EPS already 0.95x its 10y max.

name: Texas Capital Bancshares, Inc.
reason: Commercial bank mid-transformation toward an investment-banking/treasury model with highly erratic EPS (6.21 to 1.12 to 6.18 to 1.28 to 6.79) and 10y avg ROE of 8.2%, so normalised earnings power is not forecastable.

name: Carter's, Inc.
reason: Children's apparel brand in structural decline (10y EPS CAGR -2.8%, 2025 EPS -40%, margin at 4.3% vs 10.2% avg) facing falling birth rates, tariffs and wholesale share loss, with ND/EBITDA now 4.0x.

name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co.
reason: Commoditised server/storage/networking vendor with revenue -4.0%/yr over 10y, 10y avg ROIC 4.5%, acquisitions ~2x FCF (Juniper) and ND/EBITDA 4.1x; growth is acquisition- and leverage-driven, not core.

name: TD SYNNEX Corp.
reason: Thin-margin IT distributor (EBIT margin 2.3%, 10y avg ROIC 6.8%) whose 15% EPS CAGR came largely from the Tech Data merger (shares +7.7%/yr) and buybacks; a cheap but ordinary middleman without specialness.

name: Array Technologies, Inc.
reason: Solar-tracker maker dependent on utility-scale solar build cycles and IRA/tariff policy, with volatile EPS (0.93 to 0.07 to 1.13 to 0.60), 10y avg ROIC 1.3%, ND/EBITDA 3.9x and adjusted EPS ~2x GAAP.

name: The Wendy's Co.
reason: Franchised burger chain with ND/EBITDA 7.5x, flat revenue (1.5%/yr), margin at 9th pctile and consensus FY1 EPS -44%; EPS growth was buyback/leverage-driven while traffic is losing share to stronger QSR peers.

name: WEX, Inc.
reason: Fleet-card/benefits/corporate-payments mix with a good EPS record (10y CAGR 12.7%) but fuel-price-linked revenue, EV transition risk to fleet cards, acquisitions ~1.0x FCF, a deposit-funded balance sheet (10y ROIC 3.2%) and a very large adjusted-vs-GAAP gap make 10-year forecasting low-confidence.

name: Hilltop Holdings, Inc.
reason: Bank plus broker-dealer plus PrimeLending mortgage origination, so earnings are set by mortgage-rate and capital-markets cycles (EPS 4.61 in 2021 to 1.60 in 2022, now 0.42x 10y max, 10y EPS CAGR 2.4%).

name: CF Industries Holdings, Inc.
reason: Low-cost nitrogen producer, but earnings are set by nitrogen/natural-gas price spreads no one can forecast (EPS -0.25 in 2017 to 16.39 in 2022, margin 7.9%-50.1%) and consensus FY2-FY3 EPS is -24%/-21%.

name: Home Bancshares, Inc. (Arkansas)
reason: Highly efficient, founder-led bank with EPS at a 10y high ($2.35), but 10y EPS growth of 8.7% came with shares +3.7%/yr from acquisitions (Happy Bancshares), loans carry CRE/construction concentration, and consensus FY2-FY3 EPS growth of only 2.5-4.5% gives no clear organic route to >=7%/yr.

name: CNO Financial Group, Inc.
reason: Senior middle-market life/health/annuity insurer whose 12% EPS CAGR is mostly buybacks (shares -6.5%/yr) on 1.7%/yr revenue growth, with 10y avg ROIC 3.5%, spread-dependent annuities and legacy long-term-care liabilities that are hard to underwrite from outside.

name: LCI Industries
reason: Dominant RV/marine component supplier but earnings are set by the boom-bust RV build cycle (EPS 15.48 in 2022 to 2.52 in 2023, now 0.48x 10y max) with acquisitions ~0.7x FCF and ND/EBITDA 2.5x.

name: ICF International, Inc.
reason: Steady government consulting record (10y EPS CAGR 9.9%, 7/10 years >=7%) but ~70% public-sector revenue exposed to US federal spending cuts (2025 EPS -9%), acquisition-assisted growth (0.74x FCF) and ND/EBITDA 2.5x make 5-10 year forecasting low-confidence.

name: Allegiant Travel Co.
reason: Ultra-low-cost leisure airline with earnings set by fuel, capacity and labour cycles (EPS 14.26 in 2019 to -9.33 in 2020, now 0.27x 10y max, 10y EPS CAGR -11.5%), negative FCF conversion and a Sunseeker resort distraction.

name: Kaiser Aluminum Corp.
reason: Semi-fabricated aluminium processor tied to aerospace/packaging/auto cycles and metal spreads, with 10y avg ROIC 3.7%, acquisitions ~2.1x FCF (Warrick), ND/EBITDA 3.5x and EPS that fell from 6.85 to -0.14 before recovering.
